# explain multiKeyPaths interpretation — facts

## Structure and components

- [statement] An empty per-key list does not prove that the source document path contains no array. A positional key such as e.0 can read e[0] from an array without generating multiple index keys, so its multiKeyPaths entry can be empty while e is an array. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-21) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-127304 · keywords: explain multiKeyPaths interpretation · also: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/52468628/mongo-indexes-on-arrays
- [statement] multiKeyPaths is per indexed key, while isMultiKey describes the index as a whole. Thus isMultiKey: true can coexist with one key having an empty list while another key has a non-empty list; an empty list means no multikey path component is recorded for that key, not that the whole index is non-multikey. (high confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-15086 · keywords: explain multiKeyPaths interpretation · also: https://dev.to/franckpachot/mongodb-multikey-indexes-and-index-bound-optimization-ol9, https://stackoverflow.com/questions/76582798/multikey-indexing-performance-drawbacks

## How it works

- [statement] For an IXSCAN, multiKeyPaths maps each key in keyPattern to the indexed path prefix or prefixes that cause multikey expansion. For example, stock.quantity: ['stock'] identifies an array ancestor, while a compound index can have isMultiKey: true and Owner: [] because the array expansion applies to another indexed key. (high confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-15086 · keywords: explain multiKeyPaths interpretation · also: https://github.com/danielabar/mongo-performance/blob/master/README.md, https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/querying-for-all-unique-key-value-pairs-in-an-array-property-across-all-documents/207409, https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-index-usage-and-mongodb-explain-part-1/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] MongoDB issue SERVER-130777 reports a narrow resumable index-build failure where a concurrent array write can be lost from multikey state, leaving explain to report isMultiKey: false and causing a matching array document to be missed. The issue lists MongoDB 6.0.0, 7.0.0, and 8.0.0 as affected and was unresolved in code review as of 2026-10-12. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-12) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-130777 · keywords: explain multiKeyPaths interpretation

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Treat multiKeyPaths as index path metadata, not as the current query's constraints or scan range. It records array paths for the index and informs which bounds the planner can use; indexBounds shows the ranges that the IXSCAN actually searches, so read both fields together. (high confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-15086 · keywords: explain multiKeyPaths interpretation · also: https://dev.to/franckpachot/mongodb-multikey-indexes-and-index-bound-optimization-ol9, https://www.percona.com/blog/2018/09/06/mongodb-investigate-queries-with-explain-index-usage-part-2/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/, https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-index-usage-and-mongodb-explain-part-1/
